subject: ShopWave: sudden request pacing at edge causing spikes in latency and 5xx
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shopwave.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: support@shopwave.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency and 5xx spikes this morning (ShopWave storefront)

Jasmine — we started seeing elevated latency and intermittent 500/502 responses from Redwood-backed endpoint for our storefront personalization calls around 08:45 PT. Traffic volume isn't higher than normal (we're flat week-over-week), but a large portion of requests are receiving 429/500 and median p90 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1200ms.

Attached: a 30-minute request sample, request headers, and a CDN snapshot. Can you confirm if anything on Redwood's side changed (quota/pacing/burst) or if this looks like an upstream routing flap? This is affecting a high-traffic checkout path — our ops team is seeing cart abandonment.

— Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform, ShopWave
alex.turner@shopwave.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

----
Response expectations: urgent — please escalate to ops and product if needed.

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shopwave.com>, support@shopwave.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spikes this morning (ShopWave storefront)

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Alex — we're on it. Connor, Marcus — can you triage ASAP? Initial ask: confirm whether ShopWave hit a rate cap, quota window, or if a burst safety valve tripped for their account/route. If it's a policy threshold, propose an emergency rollback or temporary quota bump.

Context for triage:
- Customer uses route: /v1/generate-personalization (model: redwood-lr-1b) pinned on dedicated capacity (dedicated pool id: ded-44).
- ShopWave reports no traffic surge on their side.
- They see p90 >1s and mix of 429/500/502.

Alex — we'll keep you updated every 30 minutes. If we recommend a temporary config change that exposes cost, we'll flag it for Marissa (sales) for approval.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
AE, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shopwave.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spikes this morning (ShopWave storefront)

Quick summary from runtime traces and quota telemetry:
- We see sustained request arrival rate matching their normal profile.
- A safety gating rule applied at 08:42 PT on the dedicated pool 'ded-44' reduced the burst window from 10s to 2s; this coincided with p90 jump and 429s. The rule was triggered by a cross-tenant burst-detection policy that aggregates short-window peaks across multiple tenants.
- Additionally, their per-route token-bucket effective refill appears misaligned with the new shard-level pacing (we're enforcing a lower per-route ceiling due to a recent policy patch). Together: policy patch reduced available burst headroom and their per-route limiter started dropping tokens, which escalated into queue saturation and downstream 5xx as backpressure hit model servers.

Immediate mitigations we can take (recommended order):
1) Roll back the cross-tenant burst gating change on ded-44 (safety valve rollback) — 2-3 minute change window.
2) Bypass the per-route tighter refill for ShopWave (temporary override rule) to restore previous token-bucket params.
3) If rollback not possible quickly, route ShopWave traffic to compatible spare capacity pool ded-47 with same model family (auto-fallback path).

Risk and notes: rollback returns headroom but reduces aggregate protections for noisy neighbors; should be fine short-term while we monitor. Routing to ded-47 has small cold-cache latency for KV cache (estimated additional 40-80ms) but avoids 429s.

I'll prepare the change set and a single-click rollback. Marcus — can you validate there are no pending orchestration jobs that would conflict with the rollback? Marissa — this may incur short-term cost delta if we increase burst allowance; advise on commercial handling for today.

Connor O'Brien
SRE — Serving Runtime
connor_obrien@redwood.com

----
Logs reviewed: runtime_traces_08_42.json (excerpt), quota-telemetry-08-00-09-00.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shopwave.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spikes this morning (ShopWave storefront)

Thanks team — quick executive note and outcome for Alex and ShopWave leadership:
- Action taken at 10:15 PT: rolled back the cross-tenant burst gating for ded-44 and applied a temporary per-route override for ShopWave. Result: 429s dropped to <0.1% within five minutes and p90 returned to ~140ms.
- Fallback path to ded-47 was staged but not needed.
- Postmortem action items we own:
  * Short-term (24–72h): create a dedicated safety valve exemption process for top-tier customers to avoid collateral throttling during cross-tenant policy rollouts.
  * Mid-term (2–4 weeks): improve rollout instrumentation so a policy patch cannot simultaneously reduce burst window and per-route refill without a canary against a small set of tenants.
  * Commercial: Jasmine/Marissa will propose a goodwill credit (one-week equivalent of overage protection) and a follow-up QBR discussion.

Alex — sorry for the impact. We will share a short RCA doc by EOD tomorrow and a remediation timeline. Appreciate your patience and the logs you attached — they helped isolate the gating interaction quickly.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

----
